reason: E1 directly supports all key premises by showing that chemical heterogeneity in CoCrFeNi nanopillars leads to SFE variations, which coordinate twinning and slip to achieve ~110% uniform elongation. E3 is only tangentially related, mentioning twin formation in <110> grains but not the mechanistic link to heterogeneity or dynamic loading. E2 is irrelevant, addressing creep at high temperature. The hypothesis accurately represents E1's findings.
premises: Atomic-scale chemical heterogeneity in HEAs causes local variations in stacking fault energy (SFE).
Local SFE variations promote synergistic activation of dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
This dual mechanism delays necking and enhances uniform ductility under dynamic loading.
The effect is demonstrated in <110>-oriented CoCrFeNi nanopillars under tension.
